findings.containment: The claim concerns worldly prestige as stated in the ayah; it does not infer vanity or an intention to show off.

findings.title: Fullness beside desiccation
findings.claim: Exploratorily, the superiority field becomes lush and saturated on its visible surface, while destruction can be felt as desiccation.
findings.mechanism: Athāth's dense-growth image and the attributed satiation branch mapped to riʾya meet the rainless-land branch mapped to ahlaknā. Their contact turns visible fullness into a condition that can be stripped away by desiccation.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader can feel the contrast between saturated abundance and barren aftermath, so visible fullness reads as contingent rather than self-preserving.
findings.containment: This is a material analogy only, not the lexical sense of furnishings, appearance, or destruction; the split root mapping and reader trace remain attributed.

epistemic.reason: The HFT labels this outlier exploratory; its focus coordinates are exact, while its secondary root mapping and ecological synthesis remain legacy_unbound.
